key_insight: PDBQITE turns double-bracket imaginary-time evolution into a probabilistic, single-ancilla protocol that cuts circuit depth exponentially while preserving practical per-step success rates.
engineering_relevance: This offers a nearer-term route to ground-state preparation and hybrid quantum optimization on hardware with limited coherence, because each iteration uses only one controlled real-time evolution and one mid-circuit measurement.
method: Uses a probabilistic variant of DB-QITE with a single ancilla qubit.
Per iteration: apply one controlled real-time evolution, then measure mid-circuit.
Derives a system-size-independent lower bound on total success probability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical simulations showing per-step success probability stays close to unity, and benchmarks indicate better ground-state preparation than PITE and improved QAOA approximation ratios at equal depth on random regular graphs.
watch_item: Total success probability still decays exponentially with the number of iterations, so practical performance depends on how often the full routine must be repeated.
paper_title: A quantum double-bracket algorithm for imaginary-time evolution with exponentially shorter depth
